note: Live-session recording of the screen scenes (series/tools/rec). prepare/teardown run on the laptop, not recorded; commands are typed and run for real in Git Bash scripts via 'bash'. The 'user' screen signs in as alex.demo in a separate Azure CLI config folder (AZURE_CONFIG_DIR) so labadmin stays signed in for the other screens.
prepare: # laptop toolchain for the bash scripts: Git Bash first on PATH, python3 and zip shims in %TEMP% (the laptop has neither)

$shim = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'mgshim'; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $shim | Out-Null; [IO.File]::WriteAllText("$shim\python3", "#!/bin/bash`nexec python `"`$@`"`n"); [IO.File]::WriteAllText("$shim\zip.py", "import sys,os,zipfile`nz=zipfile.ZipFile(os.path.abspath(sys.argv[-2]),'w',zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED)`n[z.write(os.path.join(r,n),os.path.relpath(os.path.join(r,n),'.').replace(os.sep,'/')) for r,d,f in os.walk('.') for n in f]`nz.close()`n"); [IO.File]::WriteAllText("$shim\zip", "#!/bin/bash`nexec python `"`$(dirname `"`$0`")/zip.py`" `"`$@`"`n")
az account show --query name -o none 2>$null; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { az login --use-device-code }   # owner signs in as labadmin
az bicep upgrade   # Microsoft Graph Bicep needs a current Bicep CLI (Azure CLI 2.73 or newer)

screens.name: graph-deploy
screens.note: Runs as labadmin (the account that may create app registrations and app role assignments). If processorCanWrite fails with a principal-not-found error right after the identity was created, run it again (directory replication) and keep that in the episode.

screens.name: app-roles
steps: App registrations > All applications > 'contoso orders API' > App roles: show Orders.ReadWrite.All (Applications) and Orders.Reader (Users)
Optional: Expose an API (App ID URI and the Orders.Read scope with the Azure CLI as authorized client)
Certificates & secrets: show there are none (b-roll for 'zero secrets')
Enterprise applications > 'contoso orders API' > Properties: Assignment required = Yes
Users and groups: Alex Demo with Orders.Reader (the managed identity may only appear under its own Enterprise application > Permissions)
mask: tenant name in the header and tenant ID
real user names: the reader must be the fictional Alex Demo
prepare: $sp = az ad sp show --id $apiId --query id -o tsv; $role = az ad sp show --id $apiId --query "appRoles[?value=='Orders.Reader'].id | [0]" -o tsv; $alex = az ad user list --filter "startswith(userPrincipalName,'alex.demo@')" --query "[0].id" -o tsv
@{ principalId = $alex; resourceId = $sp; appRoleId = $role } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress | Set-Content "$env:TEMP\ep04-assign.json" -Encoding ascii

az rest --method POST --uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/$sp/appRoleAssignedTo" --headers "Content-Type=application/json" --body "@$env:TEMP\ep04-assign.json" -o none 2>$null   # Alex Demo becomes the Orders.Reader; deploy.sh made labadmin the reader
screens.note: Two captures side by side: App roles blade, and Enterprise application Users and groups plus Properties.

screens.name: call-as-user
prepare: bash infra/lab-preauthorize-cli.sh   # LAB ONLY, as labadmin (owner of the app): lets az request Orders.Read without a consent prompt
az login --use-device-code --allow-no-subscriptions   # owner signs in as alex.demo (the fictional reader)

for ($i = 0; $i -lt 90 -and -not (Test-NetConnection localhost -Port 5080 -WarningAction SilentlyContinue).TcpTestSucceeded; $i++) { Start-Sleep -Seconds 2 }   # the API listens on http://localhost:5080
mask: oid, tid and client ID GUIDs in the claims block
screens.note: Expected: aud = API client ID, scp = Orders.Read, roles = [Orders.Reader], kind = delegated; GET /orders 200, GET /me 200, POST /orders 403. A 401 with an audience error means a v1.0 token (see the gotcha scene).

screens.name: app-token
prepare: Remove-Item Env:AZURE_CONFIG_DIR -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue   # back to the labadmin Azure CLI session (creates the container instance)
screens.note: If the log says python3: not found, the azure-cli image changed: replace the image with a Microsoft-published Python base image, keep the same --command-line, and note it in the README.

teardown: Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -match 'run-api-local|Contoso.Orders.Api' -and $_.ProcessId -ne $PID } | ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
bash infra/teardown.sh rg-mglab-azure-04   # service principal and app deleted and purged, group deleted
az ad app list --display-name "contoso orders API" --query "[].appId" -o tsv   # nothing listed
